IN RE: DENIS J CARLSON
PETITION FOR Review for Responsible Party
PERIOD(S) 3Q10-3Q12 EMPL 6M11, 1Q12 SALES
AND NOW, May 22, 2014, pursuant to the Fiscal Code, the Act of 1929, April 9, P.L. 343,
as amended, (72 P.S. § 1 et seq), the Board of Finance and Revenue of the Commonwealth of
Pennsylvania, based upon the reasons set forth herein, hereby ORDERS the following:
Jurisdiction
This petition comes before the Board of Finance and Revenue pursuant to Section 2704
of the Tax Reform Code of 1971, as amended, 72 P.S. § 9704.
Issue
Whether Petitioner has established that he was not a responsible party for the
deficiencies of the company during the periods of assessment.
Statement of the Case
Petitioner, individually and as a partner of Sno Mountain, LP, was assessed as a
responsible party pursuant to Sections 225 and 320 of the Tax Reform Code of 1971, 72 P.S.
§ 7225 and 72 P.S. § 7320.
The assessment consisted of the 3Q10-3Q12 employer withholding taxes and the
6M11, 1Q12 sales taxes that were collected, but not remitted to the Commonwealth, plus
penalties and interest. Petitioner filed a petition with the Board of Appeals requesting
abatement or compromise of the responsible party assessment. The Board of Appeals
sustained the assessment stating that Petitioner was an owner and responsible party of Sno
Mountain, LP.
In the petition filed with the Board of Finance and Revenue, Petitioner requests
abatement of the assessment stating that he was not responsible for the employer withholding
and sales taxes of Snow Mountain, LP. Petitioner explains that he was the president and

general partner of Snow Mountain, LLC, and Snow Mountain LLC was a general partner in
Sno Mountain, LP, operating as Montage Mountain. Petitioner contends that he was a %
limited partner and unpaid creditor in Snow Mountain, LP, and as such was not responsible for
the tax liabilities of Sno Mountain, LP. Petitioner states that he had the ability to sign checks,
but the controller and general manager signed all of the checks. Petitioner claims that he had
no access to financial records and the general manager was responsible for the payroll.
The responsible party questionnaire submitted by Petitioner to the Department of
Revenue indicates that Petitioner duties and responsibilities with Sno Mountain, LP, were:
• Developing the company as both a ski resort and waterpark resort.
• Hiring and firing of personnel.
• Signing of construction projects.
• Signing contracts with vendors.
• Coordinating efforts of ski patrol.
• Overseeing conditions of facilities.
• Partnership Meetings.
• Developing Melf Schedules.
• Developed Web Page.
• Developed Microsoft programs.
Petitioner claimed that he had the authority to sign the following:
• Construction contracts.
• Vendor contracts.
• Feasibility contracts.
• Facility Purchase contracts.
• Loan Agreements.
Statement of the Law
All taxes collected by any person from purchasers in accordance with this article and all
taxes collected by any person from purchasers under color of this article which have not been
properly refunded by such person to the purchaser shall constitute a trust fund for the
Commonwealth, and such trust shall be enforceable against such person, his representatives
and any person (other than a purchaser to whom a refund has been made properly) receiving
any part of such fund without consideration, or knowing that the taxpayer is committing a
breach of trust: Provided, however, That any person receiving payment of a lawful obligation
of the taxpayer from such fund shall be presumed to have received the same in good faith and
without any knowledge of the breach of trust. Any person, other than a taxpayer, against
whom the department makes any claim under this section shall have the same right to petition
and appeal as is given taxpayers by any provisions of this part. 72 P.S. § 7225.
Every employer required to deduct and withhold tax under this article is hereby made
liable for such tax. For purposes of assessment and collection, any amount required to be
withheld and paid over to the department and any additions to tax penalties and interest with

respect thereto, shall be considered the tax of the employer. All taxes deducted and withheld
from employees pursuant to this article or under color of this article shall constitute a trust fund
for the Commonwealth and shall be enforceable against such employer, his representative or
any other person receiving any part of such fund. 72 P.S. § 7320.
In George W. Brown III, as Individual and as President of Electrical Industries, Inc. v.
Commonwealth, 670 A.2d 1222 at 1225 (Pa. Commw. Ct. 1996), the Court determined that, for
the period when the bank took total control over the taxpayer and the officer had no control
over any financial operations, regardless of the fact that the officer remained on the premises
after the bank took control, the Officer was not liable for sales and withholding taxes. The
Court concluded that the taxpayer was not an active or controlling Officer of the corporation for
the period in which the bank held complete control over the financial operations of the
company. Conversely, the Court held that the taxpayer was liable for sales and withholding
taxes for the period in which he remained active and in control of the general management of
the business, including the financial operations.
In reaching this conclusion, the Court in Brown relied on the case of City of Philadelphia
v. B. Axe Company, 40 Pa. Commw. Ct. 257, 397 A.2d 51 (1979), wherein the Court
determined:
[A] corporation collecting taxes as an agent of a municipality
and failing to pay over such taxes to the municipality is a trustee ex
maleficio, and active and controlling corporate officers are
responsible for the performance of that trust duty by the
corporation. Where such persons fail to perform that duty, the
individuals are trustees ex maleficio as well as the corporation.
Id. at 261, 397 A.2d at 53.
The court in Axe also identified several factors that it considered important in
determining whether a corporate officer and shareholder was responsible for unpaid
withholding tax: physical presence on the premises at relevant times, ability to hire and fire
employees, review and signing tax documents, signing payroll checks, signing checks for
expenses, obtaining loans, consulting the company’s books, and acting as an administrator
and manager.
Except as otherwise provided by this act, in all cases of petitions filed pursuant to this
article, the burden of proof shall be upon the petitioner or appellant, as the case may be.
72 P.S. § 9705.
Conclusion
Upon review of the facts presented, this Board finds that Petitioner has failed to show
that he was not a responsible party of Sno Mountain, LP, in regard to the company’s sales tax
and employer withholding tax obligations. Petitioner was the president and general partner of
Sno Mountain, LLC, an entity that managed Sno Mountain, LP. Petitioner was also a limited
partner of Sno Mountain, LP. Insofar as Petitioner has failed to clearly explain the relationship

was not a responsible party.
ORDER
This petition is denied.
